title: Zenwell Health - SOC 2 / ISO 27001 Posture Review
summary: Redwood team reviewed SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture, trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO options, audit logging/retention, and KMS/BYOK options. Customer asked about data residency and VPC/private deployment for PHI. Agreement to share SOC 2 report, ISO certificate, and controls mapping spreadsheet; schedule an on-prem / VPC technical deep dive with SEs; provide sample audit log format and Splunk/Datadog integration notes.
topics: SOC 2 Type II scope and report access
Trust Center access and controls mapping
Data residency and private deployment (VPC / on-prem)
Next steps: share artifacts and schedule deep dive
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time — Samir from Redwood here, I have Priya our SE and Elena from success. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Lena (Zenwell): Hi Samir, doing fine thanks. We've got a couple of folks from our security and infra team, Mark and Priya. Tommy on as well for compliance.
[00:18] Samir (Redwood): Great, the goal for today is to walk through our SOC 2 and ISO posture, answer any control-specific questions, and make sure you can access the trust center artifacts you need. We'll also touch on RBAC/SSO, logging and KMS. Does that agenda sound ok?
[00:28] Mark (Zenwell): Yep, that's perfect. We're especially interested in scope — whether PHI is covered or if we'd need a Dedicated/Private setup.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood SE): Quick intro from me — I'm Priya, I work on security and infra integrations. I'll mostly cover the technical details around network isolation, key management and logs.
[00:42] Lena (Zenwell): Cool. I pulled some of your docs earlier but wanted to confirm the SOC 2 scoping. Our main question: if we send PHI into Redwood hosted inference, is that included in SOC 2 scope or do we need Private?
[00:55] Priya (Redwood SE): Good question. Short answer: our hosted environment is SOC 2 Type II for the control environment across our multi-tenant API, but PHI handling has additional contractual and architectural constraints. For PHI we typically recommend either Redwood Dedicated with a contractual addendum or the Redwood Private deployment that sits in your VPC / on-prem. Note the report will show our control coverage for production infra, but we can't provide a SOC 2 attestation that covers customer-managed keys or customer network isolation unless it's the Private deployment.
[01:20] Tommy (Zenwell): When you say "Private deployment" — that's the VPC option where Redwood's control plane is still in your account, right?
[01:27] Priya (Redwood SE): Slight correction — our Private deployment option can be run in a customer VPC or on-prem where the control plane access is limited; there's an option for customer-managed control plane (for enterprise) or a hybrid where we operate but with separate tenancy. We'll share the architecture diagram.
[01:40] Mark (Zenwell): OK. For compliance we'll need the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 cert, and a controls mapping that maps your controls to our internal policy — AICPA controls mapping or similar. Do you provide that out of the trust center?
[01:53] Samir (Redwood): Yes — we provide a Trust Center portal where customers with an NDA can access the SOC 2 report, ISO certificate, pen test summaries and a controls mapping spreadsheet (we map our controls to common frameworks). We'll send a link after this call. Note that access requires customer SSO to be set up and a simple request form.
[02:08] Lena (Zenwell): Great. Is the controls mapping a machine-readable sheet? We usually ingest it into our GRC tooling.
[02:14] Elena (Redwood CSM): The mapping is a spreadsheet (CSV/Excel) with columns for control ID, description, control owner, evidence artifact links and scope notes. It should be ingestible into most GRC tools.
[02:28] Mark (Zenwell): On audit logs — what do they look like and can we forward them to Splunk/Datadog? Retention?
[02:35] Priya (Redwood SE): We emit structured audit logs for API calls, admin actions, and model deployments. Format is JSON with fields for request_id, user_id (Redwood principal), customer_project_id, operation, timestamp, latency, model_variant. We have a log forwarding mechanism to push to an S3 bucket or push via TLS to a SIEM endpoint — customers commonly forward to Splunk/Datadog via our collector. Retention in the managed service is 90 days by default; we have enterprise options for longer retention. We'll share the schema example.
[03:05] Tommy (Zenwell): We need 1 year for certain logs for PHI retention compliance. Can Redwood accommodate that?
[03:12] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, on Dedicated/Private we can extend retention and ship logs to your pre-configured S3 with lifecycle policies you control. For hosted, we have add-on packages for extended retention but for PHI we usually recommend Private so you control the retention SLAs.
[03:28] Lena (Zenwell): About encryption — is the data encrypted at rest and in flight? How about KMS / BYOK?
[03:35] Priya (Redwood SE): All data in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. At rest we use envelope encryption; root keys are managed in our KMS. For enterprise customers we support BYOK (bring your own key) with integration to customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or HSM-backed keys. In Private deployments you can own the root key entirely. We'll include details in the KMS integration guide.
[04:00] Mark (Zenwell): If we use BYOK on hosted, does Redwood still have access to the plaintext or cached KVs?
[04:08] Priya (Redwood SE): With BYOK we manage ephemeral decryption keys in-memory on the runtime nodes; we do not persist plaintext to disk. For KV cache — the edge caches are encrypted and keys are rotated. Full assurance for key custody is strongest in Private where keys never leave your environment. We'll include the keyflow diagram.
[04:28] Mark (Zenwell): What about RBAC and SSO — we need SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Also role separation for engineers vs ops.
[04:36] Samir (Redwood): We support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Our RBAC allows organization-level roles, project-level roles and API key scopes. We also have admin audit trails. We can show the role matrix and default role templates.
[04:50] Priya (Redwood SE): A note on API keys — we support scoped service tokens that are least-privilege. For longer lived machine-to-machine tokens, we recommend rotating them via our token rotation API or integrate with your secret manager.
[05:05] Lena (Zenwell): We may want to integrate Redwood logs into our Splunk instance and have SSO through Okta. Okta + SCIM works?
[05:12] Samir (Redwood): Yes, Okta is supported; we'll provide a step-by-step for SAML and SCIM.
[05:19] Mark (Zenwell): Any third-party penetration test info? We need the high level results not the raw report.
[05:25] Elena (Redwood CSM): We publish a pen test summary in the Trust Center and high-level remediation status. For customers with NDA we can share the full executive summary and some evidence.
[05:36] Tommy (Zenwell): For ISO 27001 — is the scope global or only certain services?
[05:41] Priya (Redwood SE): ISO scope covers our hosted inference platform and control plane for production services. The certificate includes version and scope specifics — we'll attach the certificate and scope statement in the Trust Center. For Private deployments the certificate isn't applied to customer-managed on-prem infra unless we operate it under contract.
[06:00] Mark (Zenwell): Are there any known drift areas where you are working to remediate controls? We need to evaluate residual risk.
[06:06] Samir (Redwood): We maintain a risk register; known workstreams are around supply-chain attestations for some third-party GPUs and further MFA hardening for certain internal admin paths. These are tracked in our SOC documentation and the roadmap.
[06:20] Lena (Zenwell): Network segmentation — do you offer VPC peering or privatelink equivalents? We want to ensure traffic does not traverse the public internet.
[06:28] Priya (Redwood SE): For Dedicated/Private we offer VPC peering and private endpoints. Hosted public API uses HTTPS, but traffic can be sent over private connect with partner cloud providers for lower-latency private network. We'll include the network options doc.
[06:45] Mark (Zenwell): What about model provenance and verification — we need to know where model artifacts are stored and their supply chain pedigree.
[06:51] Priya (Redwood SE): We maintain a model catalog with provenance metadata — model source, build reproducibility, and hash fingerprints. That's part of our onboarding docs; we'll surface the catalog export for you.
[07:05] Speaker 4: (unidentified): Sorry — quick clarifying question on retention — if we request deletion for a customer dataset, how fast is it removed from caches and backups?
[07:14] Priya (Redwood SE): Good question. We have a documented data deletion workflow. For cached prefix/KV entries we purge or mark for deletion and rotate keys; for backups there is a 30-90 day window depending on the system for immutable backups, and we provide deletion certificates for primary storage. We'll send the deletion SLA matrix.
[07:36] Mark (Zenwell): Do you have SOC 2 controls mapping to HITRUST or HIPAA for PHI-specific controls?
[07:44] Samir (Redwood): We provide a controls mapping that maps SOC 2 and ISO 27001 to HIPAA control families; for HITRUST we have guidance but full HITRUST certification is not in place. We can outline the gap analysis.
[07:58] Lena (Zenwell): For the trust center access — is that automated or do you have to provision access manually?
[08:03] Elena (Redwood CSM): There's a request form and we typically provision trust center access within one business day after NDA. We'll send the link and next steps.
[08:14] Priya (Redwood SE): I'll call out one more technical caveat: if you plan to use our streaming API with very low-latency, some telemetry (metrics, trace IDs) may flow through our observability pipeline; those are covered by SOC 2 but for maximum isolation we recommend Dedicated.
[08:33] Mark (Zenwell): Okay. Onboarding timeline — if we wanted to start a pilot with non-PHI data, how quickly can we get a sandbox?
[08:40] Samir (Redwood): We can spin up a sandbox project in hosted within a day. For Dedicated it's a weeks-long setup depending on capacity and contractual lead time. Private on-prem will be longer.
[08:52] Tommy (Zenwell): Do you sign BAA for PHI?
[08:56] Samir (Redwood): Yes, we do sign a BAA for PHI and have customers under BAA on Dedicated/Private. We'll share a redlined template for your legal team.
[09:06] Lena (Zenwell): Are there any out-of-scope items we should be aware of?
[09:10] Priya (Redwood SE): Out-of-scope items typically include customer-managed apps running in their environment, or any third-party integrations you install that are outside Redwood's control plane. We'll document the exact scoping notes.
[09:22] Mark (Zenwell): One last thing — can we get sample audit events for admin changes and user activity? That will help our SIEM correlation.
[09:29] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we'll include sample JSON events and an example Splunk ingestion dashboard in the artifacts.
[09:38] Samir (Redwood): Great — I think that's most of the big questions. Any other items from anyone?
[09:43] Lena (Zenwell): Not from me. Maybe a question on legal timeline — when can you share the SOC 2 report?
[09:48] Elena (Redwood CSM): We'll provision Trust Center access today; once you accept the NDA you'll be able to download the SOC 2 Type II within the portal.
[09:57] Mark (Zenwell): Perfect.
[10:00] Samir (Redwood): Ok summarizing next steps — we'll share the Trust Center link, SOC 2 and ISO cert, controls mapping CSV, KMS integration guide, sample audit logs, and a whiteboard architecture for Private/VPC. We'll schedule a technical deep dive with Priya and your infra team next week.
[10:15] Tommy (Zenwell): Sounds good — can Priya include the keyflow diagram for BYOK and the deletion SLA?
[10:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, I'll attach both.
[10:24] Lena (Zenwell): Thanks everyone.
[10:26] Samir (Redwood): Thanks — we'll follow up via email with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the deep dive. Have a good one.
[10:32] (call ends)
